title: In Psalms 105 In What Ways Does The Story Of Joseph Illustrate Gods Sovereignty Over Our Circumstances
paragraphs: The Story of Joseph in Psalm 105: A Portrait of God's Sovereignty

Psalm 105 is a majestic recounting of God's faithfulness to His covenant people, Israel. One of the key figures highlighted in this Psalm is Joseph, whose life story provides a profound illustration of God’s sovereignty over human circumstances. Let’s explore how the narrative of Joseph, as referenced in Psalm 105, reveals God’s supreme control and purposeful guidance in the lives of His people.
Joseph’s Story in Psalm 105
Psalm 105:16-22 briefly recounts Joseph’s journey from suffering to exaltation:

And he called for a famine upon the land; He brake the whole staff of bread. He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold for a servant: His feet they hurt with fetters: He was laid in chains of iron, Until the time that his word came to pass, The word of Jehovah tried him. The king sent and loosed him; Even the ruler of peoples, and let him go free. He made him lord of his house, And ruler of all his substance; To bind his princes at his pleasure, And teach his elders wisdom. - Psalm 105:16-22 ASV
God's Sovereignty in Joseph’s Life
God Orchestrates Events for His Purpose

Joseph’s journey to Egypt was not accidental. The Psalmist states, “He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold for a servant.” Even the betrayal by Joseph’s brothers and his enslavement were under God’s sovereign hand. Though humans intended evil, God intended it for good (Genesis 50:20 ASV). God’s plan was to save many lives and preserve His covenant people through Joseph’s leadership in Egypt.
God Works Through Suffering

Joseph’s suffering—bound in chains, imprisoned unjustly—was not outside God’s control. The Psalm says, “His feet they hurt with fetters: He was laid in chains of iron, Until the time that his word came to pass, The word of Jehovah tried him.” God used suffering to refine Joseph’s character and prepare him for greater service. This echoes the New Testament teaching that God uses trials to produce steadfastness in believers (James 1:2-4 ASV).
God Exalts According to His Timing

Joseph’s release came at God’s appointed time—“the king sent and loosed him.” God raised Joseph to a position of great authority, making him “lord of his house.” This demonstrates God’s sovereign timing: He exalts and humbles according to His will (Psalm 75:7 ASV).
God Uses Individuals for the Good of Many

Joseph’s wisdom was used to save nations from famine, to “teach his elders wisdom,” and to fulfill God’s promises to Abraham’s descendants. In this, Joseph’s life prefigures Christ, who also suffered unjustly and was exalted for the salvation of many (Philippians 2:8-11 ASV).
Insights for Believers Today

Joseph’s story, as highlighted in Psalm 105, assures believers that even when circumstances seem chaotic or unjust, God is at work. His sovereignty means He is able to take what humans mean for evil and accomplish His good purposes. Believers can trust that God is working “all things together for good” for those who love Him (Romans 8:28 ASV).
Conclusion

The story of Joseph in Psalm 105 is a powerful reminder that God is always in control, orchestrating every detail of our lives according to His perfect will. Even in suffering and uncertainty, we can be confident in His sovereign purposes and His unfailing faithfulness.
